title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is Grothendieck's 1986 'Analysis situs' (fourth draft), which develops a combinatorial 'tame topology'. The page treats the one-dimensional base case. L is a totally ordered set, the model 'line'. 'Préfigures' are the tame subsets of L, i.e. finite unions of points and intervals. 'Figures' are the closed ones. 'Polygones' (in M) appear on the next page.

First lines (end of the lemma from the previous page). Let Φ, Ψ be connected prefigures. Then Φ and Ψ are the connected components of Φ∪Ψ (i.e. Φ∪Ψ is disconnected, Φ∩Ψ=∅, and the two pieces are not glued, not 'recollés') iff Φ <! Ψ or Ψ <! Φ. Here <! means 'strictly before and separated': not adjacent in a way that makes the union connected, as [0,1) and [1,2] would be. Equivalently, {Φ,Ψ} is a flag (chain) for <! in Préfig conn(M).

Recapitulative theorem.

1) Classification of connected prefigures. Take a nonempty flag 𝔻 in L. Effectively only its extremes matter, so 𝔻 is a point or a pair a<b. Define the margin boundary ∂𝔻 = ∅ if card 𝔻 = 1, and {inf 𝔻, sup 𝔻} if card 𝔻 ≥ 2. Let F_𝔻 be the closed figure determined by 𝔻: the point {a}, or the segment [a,b]. For α ⊂ ∂𝔻, set Φ_{𝔻,α} = F_𝔻 \ α. The map (𝔻,α) ↦ Φ_{𝔻,α} is a bijection onto the connected prefigures: points, [a,b], [a,b), (a,b], (a,b).

2) Closedness and openness. Φ is a figure (closed) iff α = ∅. For openness, first assume L has no least or greatest element: Φ is open iff card 𝔻 ≥ 2 and α = ∂𝔻. In general, let Θ ⊂ L be the set of extremal elements of L, of cardinality 0, 1 or 2. Then Φ is open iff card 𝔻 ≥ 2 and α = ∂𝔻 \ (∂𝔻 ∩ Θ). The next page says 'connexe', but 'ouverte' is clearly meant.

3) (Next page.) Every prefigure or polygon is uniquely a disjoint union of a <!-chain of connected ones; these are its connected components. So D ↦ ∪D is a bijection Drap*_{<!}(conn) → all.

Purpose: a purely order-theoretic, combinatorial description of tame subsets of a line and of their closed, open and connected members. This is the base step before higher-dimensional 'polyhedral/semi-algebraic' figures. Mathematically it is the one-dimensional cell decomposition familiar from o-minimality.
errors: Statement 2, as continued on the next page, reads 'Φ est connexe ssi card D ≥ 2 et α = ∂D − (∂D∩Θ)'. By construction every Φ_{D,α} is connected, so this must be a slip for 'ouverte'.

For (D,α) ↦ Φ_{D,α} to be a bijection, D must be determined by its extremes (card ≤ 2), or else F_D must only depend on inf and sup. With arbitrary longer flags the map is not injective. The draft leaves this implicit.

The bijection onto all connected prefigures also implicitly excludes unbounded intervals (rays). That is fine if prefigures are bounded by elements of L, or if L is assumed to have endpoints adjoined. The page does not say.

ideas.what: Classification of connected tame subsets of a totally ordered line as intervals, indexed by an endpoint set D plus a subset α of its boundary that is removed
ideas.modern_name: intervals in a dense linear order; 1-dimensional cells in o-minimal cell decomposition
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical; o-minimal framework by van den Dries (1984), Pillay–Steinhorn (1986)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) only calls for a 'topologie modérée'; no such details

ideas.what: Criterion for openness of an interval taking account of the extremal elements Θ of L
ideas.modern_name: open intervals in the order topology, including half-rays at endpoints

ideas.what: Separation relation <! between connected pieces (strictly before and not glued); decomposition of an arbitrary prefigure as a <!-chain (flag) of connected components
ideas.modern_name: decomposition of a definable subset of a line into finitely many disjoint, non-adjacent intervals and points (connected components)
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore / o-minimal monotonicity and cell decomposition

missed.claim: This is an unpublished, fully combinatorial (flag-theoretic) foundation of one-dimensional tame topology from 1986. It was contemporaneous with, and independent of, the o-minimality papers. It documents that Grothendieck's 'topologie modérée' programme was being built from ordered-set combinatorics (flags, the separation relation <!, the boundary ∂D) rather than from model theory. The mathematics is elementary; the historical record of this approach is what is missing.
missed.quote: Pour tout 𝔻 ∈ Drap*(L), et toute partie α de ∂𝔻 ... soit Φ_{𝔻,α} = F_𝔻 \ α ... On trouve ainsi une bijection
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is of historical interest for the relationship between the Esquisse's tame-topology programme and o-minimality. It is not new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is the elementary classification of intervals and of tame subsets of an ordered line. It is a standard result, though phrased in Grothendieck's own flag formalism. Its only interest is as documentation of his 1986 analysis-situs programme.
transcription_corrections: 'Préfig comm(M)' should read 'Préfig conn(M)' (connected prefigures), and 'l'ens. des préfigures communes' should read 'préfigures connexes'.
Opening line is likely 'et Ψ soient les composantes connexes de Φ∪Ψ, i.e. Φ∪Ψ déconnecté(e), il faut et suffit que Φ <! Ψ ou Ψ <! Φ'.

'Pour que Φ soit ouverte, il f. et s., sous condition (Hyp) ... et on suppose que L n'a ni plus petit ni plus grand élément, que card 𝔻 ≥ 2 et α = ∂𝔻.' The '[?] par le plus petit ou le plus grand' is likely 'n'a pas de plus petit ni de plus grand'.
Last lines are likely 'En éliminant cette Hyp. et sans préjuger s'il existe un plus petit ou un plus grand élément dans L ...'.
'petit[?] [?] récapitulative' is likely 'la petite proposition récapitulative' ('En résumé, on trouve donc la petite proposition récapitulative').
On the next page, 'Φ est connexe ssi' should mathematically be 'Φ est ouverte ssi'.
